clue.text: Gallon cask housed by farmer for peat constituent

indicators.note: something housed by another sits inside it, so the farmer's word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a Boer is a South African farmer of Dutch descent
a butt is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps a gallon barrel in his shed while cutting peat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housed by' puts G and BUTT inside BOER, Afrikaans for farmer and a standard crossword stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog butter is a fatty substance, often ancient buried butter, found preserved in peat bogs, so it is literally part of the peat.

clue.text: Couch hostility before following shrink?

indicators.note: the hostility word comes before the letter for following, fixing the order of the last two pieces

parts.note: a couch is a bed to lie on
war is open hostility
F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'p. 20 f.'

explanation.surface: A psychiatric session: the couch, then a fight, then a trip to the shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts BEDWAR ahead of F. 'Couch' and 'shrink' set up a psychiatrist's office, but shrink is a verb: to bedwarf is to make small, an old word in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedwarf something is to make it dwarfish, to stunt or diminish it, which is a way of making it shrink.

clue.text: Carousal in Perth? Useless to grumble — drink up

parts.note: read as USE-less: grouse, to grumble, with the letters of use taken out

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the drink's letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nog is a drink, as in eggnog

explanation.surface: Advice at a drinking party: no point complaining, just finish your drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Useless' splits as USE-less, telling you to strip USE from GROUSE; 'up' reads the drink upwards in this down clue, giving GON. Perth looks Scottish but is the Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang uses grog for any liquor, and a grog-on is a party given over to drinking it.

clue.text: Drum and guitar's intro interrupting rock superstar

indicators.note: the guitar's opening letter breaks into the singer's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of the rock band U2

indicators.note: a guitar's intro is its opening, so only the first letter of guitar is used

parts.note: guitar's intro is its first letter, G

explanation.surface: A band's drummer and guitarist cut in while their famous singer is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is a small hand drum, usually played in pairs, so it is one kind of drum.

clue.text: Water flow regulator, new, installed by complete duffer

indicators.note: the letter for new is installed in the duffer's word, put inside it

parts.note: a turkey is slang for a hopeless person or a total flop

explanation.surface: A useless plumber fits a brand-new tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed by' puts N inside TURKEY. Chambers lists turnkey also in the sense of turncock, a tap or valve for regulating the flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncock is a stopcock that controls flow, and Chambers gives turnkey as a name for it as well as for a jailer.

clue.text: Work adequately matched rising rate

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to have met a standard is to have matched it adequately

explanation.surface: A worker's output did just keep pace with a climbing rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or rate at which music is played or events move.

clue.text: Those leading in the best type of rock

indicators.note: the leaders' word goes inside the word for the best

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group
the van, short for vanguard, are those leading an advance

explanation.surface: The leaders sit among the finest examples of a sort of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal. 'Rock' looks like music after the bongo, but it is geology.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvanite, or elvan, is a Cornish quartz-porphyry, a granite-like dyke rock.

clue.text: The US take advantage of struggling pound, investing millions (6, two words)

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the rearranged letters enclose the letter for millions
something struggling is in disarray, so the letters of pound are shuffled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Americans exploit a weak pound by pouring in millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges POUND to DUPON, and 'investing' wraps it round M. 'The US' marks the definition as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, to dump on someone is to treat them badly or exploit them, a sense of taking advantage of.

clue.text: Golf course employee, one responsible for many extras?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... looks after a golf course
second meaning: an inexperienced wicketkeeper in cricket lets through many byes, which are extras

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and byes that pass the wicketkeeper are one kind; a green (novice) keeper concedes plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenkeeper tends the greens and grounds of a golf course; split, a green keeper is a raw wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Hitler's dream? He made list possibly

indicators.note: possibly says that 'He made list' rearranged would give Hitler's dream, so the letters of one are those of the other

parts.note: the composite fodder: its letters equal the answer's plus those of made list
these letters, with the answer's, make up the letters of Hitler's dream

explanation.surface: A wry reading of Nazi ambitions: perhaps the Führer's fantasy was drawing up a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'He + made list, possibly rearranged, gives Hitler's dream': 'possibly' is the anagram signal. Strip MADELIST from HITLERSDREAM and HERR is left, so 'He' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German title for a man, the equivalent of Mr, so a German he is a Herr.

clue.text: Membrane or last of quinsy restricting part of throat, forming clots

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the outer pieces hold the throat word inside them

parts.note: a coat is a covering layer or membrane, as in the coats of the eye
taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of quinsy is taken

parts.note: the last letter of quinsy is Y
the gula is the upper part of the throat or gullet

explanation.surface: A medical note: a membrane at the end of a quinsy is narrowing the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes Y from quinsy, and 'restricting' has COATORY hold GULA. Quinsy is a throat abscess, so the medical scene fits clotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Coagulatory describes what causes or relates to coagulation, the thickening of blood into clots.

clue.text: A ruler, OE, excited when dressing queen in French cloak

indicators.note: the rearranged letters dress, or clothe, the queen's letters, wrapping round them
excited letters are stirred up, so A RULER OE is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
QU is the abbreviation for queen in Chambers

explanation.surface: A ruler, rather worked up, helps the queen into a French cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges A RULER OE to ROELAURE, and 'dressing' has it wrap round QU, the Chambers abbreviation for queen, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roquelaure is an 18th-century knee-length cloak named after the French Duc de Roquelaure.

clue.text: Duvet to suffice covering one

parts.note: to do is to be enough, as in 'that will do'
on means placed upon, covering
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A single duvet ought to be enough cover for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Doona is Australian, from a trade name, for a continental quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Doona is the Australian word for a quilt or continental quilt.

clue.text: End broken off, displace back bone, thin and flat

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in reverse order
the final letter of the word for displace is broken off

parts.note: to remove something is to displace it

explanation.surface: An injury report: a bone in the back snapped, one end broken off and displaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End broken off' cuts REMOVE to REMOV, and 'back' reverses it. 'Back bone' reads as spine, but bone starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The vomer is the thin flat bone forming part of the nasal septum, the partition inside the nose.

clue.text: Estate car, lurid in colour but good to travel in

indicators.note: the final 'in' says the good and travel letters go inside the colour word

parts.note: lurid can mean ghastly pale, and wan is pale in colour
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: An estate car may be garishly painted, but it is good to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'in' is the containment signal; the first belongs to 'lurid in colour'. Lurid usually means garish, but its older sense is pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives waggon, or wagon, as a word for an estate car, a station wagon.

clue.text: Spoil daily accepting money?

indicators.note: the paper accepts, or takes in, the money letter

parts.note: a daily is a daily newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Does a daily newspaper spoil its readers by taking bribes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' and 'accepting money' suggest corruption, but spoil means indulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to overindulge someone, which is to spoil them.

clue.text: No stranger to redundancy, among people on a strike

indicators.note: the answer is found among the letters of people on a strike, running across the words

parts.note: the answer runs through peoPLE ON A STrike

explanation.surface: Workers on strike know all about being laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' says the answer sits within the words. Redundancy looks like job losses beside a strike, but here it means using more words than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleonast is someone who habitually uses pleonasm, superfluous verbal repetition, so verbal excess is familiar to them.

clue.text: Bantus in pursuit stun African antelope

indicators.note: the Bantus follow, chasing behind, so their word comes after the stun letters

parts.note: KO is a knockout, a blow that stuns
the Ngoni are a Bantu people of southern Africa

explanation.surface: Bantu hunters chase and stun an African antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The kongoni is a hartebeest of East Africa, a large antelope species.

clue.text: After single, member of gang possibly returns to crease

indicators.note: the reversed animal comes after the single, fixing the order

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run

indicators.note: returns means the animal's letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: gang is a collective noun for elk, so an elk is one member

explanation.surface: A cricketer takes a single, and a gang member hurries back to the batting crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' gives KLE and 'After' sets it last. The cricket surface makes crease the batting line, but it means a wrinkle; runkle is Scots for one, and gang is a collective noun for elk.
explanation.definitionFit: A runkle is a Scottish word for a wrinkle or crumple, a crease in cloth or skin.

clue.text: Place for a drink and what that might be with German ignoring queue?

parts.note: a bar is where drinks are served
the drink served there might be gin

explanation.surface: At a crowded bar, a German pushes past everyone waiting to order his drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Barging means pushing in rudely, so someone barging in jumps ahead of a waiting line.

clue.text: Aussie drunk, very smelly, no saint

indicators.note: no means the saint's letters are taken away

parts.note: stinky means very smelly

explanation.surface: An Australian drinker who reeks and is certainly no saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky is Australian slang for intoxicated, an adjective meaning drunk.

clue.text: River diverted, lake's dry wretchedly, refreshed liquidly no longer

indicators.note: wretchedly means the letters are in a bad way, rearranged once the river letter has been diverted

parts.note: the anagram fodder, which holds the answer's letters plus the river letter

explanation.surface: With the river diverted, the lake has run miserably dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' draws R off, and 'wretchedly' rearranges what is left of LAKESDRY. 'No longer' marks the answer as archaic: Spenser's past participle of slake.
explanation.definitionFit: Yslaked is an obsolete form of slaked, and slaked means having had one's thirst quenched with drink.

clue.text: What trappers were after, left to prepare traps?

indicators.note: the word for prepare traps, or encloses, the letter for left

parts.note: to fix a meal is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A trapper heads off to set the traps for the fur they were seeking.
explanation.definitionFit: Flix is an old word for fur or the down of a beaver, the pelts that trappers hunted.

clue.text: Travel lodge? Maria singularly takes refuge in it

indicators.note: taking refuge in means sheltering inside, so the lunar sea word goes inside it

parts.note: maria are the dark seas on the moon; the singular is mare

explanation.surface: A traveller named Maria shelters in a roadside motel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes refuge in' signals containment. 'Maria' looks like a woman's name; it is the plural of the Latin word for the dark seas on the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaret is a Turkish hospice or inn for pilgrims and travellers, a lodge on the road.

clue.text: No longer together, son makes up for shortcomings

parts.note: atone is an obsolete form of 'at one', meaning together

explanation.surface: After a separation, a son tries to make up for his failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer together' sounds like a break-up, but it marks an archaic sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, which is making up for one's faults.

clue.text: Carter's lad travellin' northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue going northwards means reading the letters upwards

parts.note: repping, with the g dropped, is working as a travelling sales rep

explanation.surface: A carter's boy out on the road heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reads REPPIN upwards; the dropped g in the clue matches the dropped g in reppin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines a nipper as a boy who assists a carter or costermonger, as well as any small child.

clue.text: Rich embroidery (not new) winding round old pulpit

indicators.note: the shortened winding word goes round the pulpit word
not means the letter for new is dropped

parts.note: a turn is a winding or bend
an ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early Christian churches

explanation.surface: Ornate needlework, no longer new, is wrapped round an ancient pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tambour is embroidery worked on a drum-shaped frame, a richly textured form of needlework.

clue.text: Lichen: Nebraska's where you'll find it

indicators.note: where points to the place that holds Nebraska, so the state's letters sit inside that place's letters

parts.note: Nebraska is to be found in the USA
NE is the postal abbreviation for Nebraska

explanation.surface: A note on the habitat of a lichen growing in Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' says NE is located inside the country you'll find it in; a state is found within its country.
explanation.definitionFit: Usnea is a genus of lichens, the beard lichens that hang from trees.

clue.text: Mountain pass the Scots have found captivating you and me

indicators.note: to captivate is to capture, so the Scots word holds you and me captive inside it

parts.note: hae is Scots for have
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A Scottish mountain pass that charmed the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A hause is a northern English and Scots word for a col or narrow neck between hills.

clue.text: Foxing well-known septet maybe interrupted by cheers

indicators.note: the septet word is broken into by the cheers word

parts.note: the seven deadly sins are a famous group of seven
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A famous seven-piece band is interrupted by applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' signals containment; the septet is the seven deadly sins. Foxing is the brown spotting on old paper, not trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxing is brownish discolouration on old books and prints, a pattern of stains.

clue.text: Monkey dropping in for palm cereal

indicators.note: dropping means the letters of in are let fall from the monkey word

parts.note: a sagoin is a small South American monkey, a marmoset

explanation.surface: A monkey drops in to eat cereal from a palm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from the pith of the sago palm, used as a cereal food in puddings.

clue.text: Spirit in bottle causing endless dismay after good rub initially

indicators.note: the shortened dismay word comes after the first two letters
initially picks only the first letter of rub

parts.note: rub initially is its first letter, R

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: to appal is to dismay

explanation.surface: A bottle of spirits, causing dismay after a good massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, a spirit bought by the bottle.

clue.text: One old tar capsizing major vessel

parts.note: A means one

indicators.note: capsizing overturns the sailor word, jumbling its letters

explanation.surface: An old sailor overturns a large ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' turns TAR over into RTA. 'Vessel' looks like a ship beside tar and capsizing; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Tent erected in wood (no one inside)

indicators.note: the erected word goes in the shortened wood
no says a letter is removed from the wood word
inside says the removed letter is one from the middle

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
A means one
something erected is put up

explanation.surface: A tent is pitched in the woods with nobody inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tupek is an Inuit summer tent made of skins, a portable shelter.

clue.text: Convert from granite a form of Eire gneiss

indicators.note: a form of signals that the letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A geologist's note: transforming Irish rock from granite into gneiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a form of' rearranges EIRE GNEISS. Gneiss and granite set a geology scene, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To greisenise is to alter granite into greisen, a rock of quartz and mica, by hot vapours.

clue.text: Ancient earthwork in original condition? One's amazed

definitions.note: one who is amazed is staggered: the definition is an adjective standing for the answer

indicators.note: the earthwork word sits in the condition word

parts.note: sted is the original, Old and Middle English, form of stead, a situation or condition
an agger is a Roman embankment, especially one carrying a road

explanation.surface: Finding a Roman earthwork still intact leaves an archaeologist astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment; 'original' flags the Old and Middle English spelling of stead, which can mean a condition or situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be staggered is to be astonished or overwhelmed by surprise.
